name: Sumiyoshi
tagline: Otemachi in 12 minutes and Tokyo in 16 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Koto City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 12 minutes to Otemachi, 26 minutes to Shinjuku, 30 minutes to Shibuya and 31 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 0.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.4 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 0.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0 m to 1.4 m, a difference of 1.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 8 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 15 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is あそか病院, about 6 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 都立墨東病院, about 12 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line run through it. Toei Shinjuku Line also call here. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Toei Shinjuku Line runs at 152% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 西大島→住吉, which includes this station. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line runs at 111% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 渋谷→表参道, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000 and 2LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. What holds the figure down: a large projected flood depth. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Sumiyoshi is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Sumiyoshi. Kikukawa has only the Toei Shinjuku Line, so Sumiyoshi is the better connected. To Otemachi, for instance, Kikukawa takes 7 minutes longer. On safety, though, Kikukawa comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Kinshicho is ahead on the number of lines and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Sumiyoshi. Kinshicho also has the JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) and JR Sobu Main Line, which Sumiyoshi does not. With more lines, Kinshicho is the better connected of the two. To Shinagawa, for instance, Kinshicho is 8 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
